provenance: A DECISION TABLE, not a captured counterpart. Placement eligibility is a pure
internal decision with no external contract to capture from, so these rows are
authored directly from P1-E17-W4-S37-T1's stated rules and each names the rule it
encodes. They are never regenerated from the engine's own output: a row is changed
only by changing the rule it cites, which is why every row carries a 'rule' field.
The fleet-state and trust filters have their own focused tests; this table exists to
pin the COMBINATIONS, where an ordering mistake between filters would otherwise hide.

cases.name: every filter clear
cases.rule: a reachable, connected, undrained node reporting every required capability is eligible

cases.name: order is preserved for the router
cases.rule: the eligible set is returned in candidate order so the router sees a deterministic set

cases.name: one missing capability excludes
cases.rule: a node must report ALL required capabilities, not some

cases.name: capability match is exact, never a prefix
cases.rule: a capability is a name from a shared vocabulary, not a pattern

cases.name: no required capabilities still applies every other filter
cases.rule: an empty requirement set demands nothing of capabilities and bypasses nothing else

cases.name: local-only work is eligible nowhere
cases.rule: local-only work never runs on an enrolled node regardless of capability match or tier

cases.name: unresolvable sensitivity is treated as local-only
cases.rule: an unrecognized sensitivity resolves most restrictively

cases.name: restricted work needs at least worker-trusted
cases.rule: restricted work clears worker-trusted and controller, never paired-device

cases.name: only reachable presence places
cases.rule: unknown, unavailable and remote-via-route are all not placeable

cases.name: only an up tunnel places
cases.rule: placement can only target nodes the controller is connected to right now

cases.name: an empty fleet is a placement failure
cases.rule: an empty eligible set is always an error, never a silent fallback
